stories.summary: Arsenal remain in contact with the camp of Real Madrid winger Rodrygo as a potential long-term target Transfer talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Real Madrid winger Rodrygo is still on the shortlist of options for Arsenal, while PSV Eindhoven midfielder Paul Wanner has emerged as a target for Liverpool. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Arsenal remain in contact with the camp of Real Madrid winger Rodrygo as a potential long-term target, according to TEAMtalk. The Brazil international, 25, is currently recovering from a serious knee injury with a targeted return around December, while the Gunners are still looking to bolster their wide options following the summer departures of Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard.

- PSV Eindhoven midfielder Paul Wanner has emerged as a target for Liverpool, according to Christian Falk. The 20-year-old former Bayern Munich player has made 40 appearances since moving to the Netherlands last summer, with Bayern currently not planning to trigger his return to Munich.

- Liverpool are also among several Premier League clubs monitoring Fiorentina midfielder Cher Ndour, TEAMtalk reports. The 22-year-old has made 62 appearances since joining the Italian side from PSG in February, with Aston Villa, Newcastle United, Brighton & Hove Albion, Crystal Palace, and Hull City also credited with an interest.

- Everton are unlikely to revisit their pursuit of Tottenham forward Richarlison after a proposed summer move collapsed, according to Football Insider. The 29-year-old remains contracted to Spurs until next summer but was omitted from their Premier League squad, with subsequent moves to Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama also failing to materialize.

- Málaga are closing in on an agreement to sign free agent forward Anthony Martial following his departure from Liga MX side Monterrey, reports Foot Mercato. The former Manchester United and Sevilla forward has reportedly turned down a two-year, €10 million offer from Al Ittihad Tripoli of Libya to prioritize discussions with the Spanish club.

Other rumors
- Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester City are monitoring Roma forward Donyell Malen, who has recorded 21 goals and four assists in 25 appearances since moving to Serie A. (Ekrem Konur)

- Bayern Munich are keeping tabs on Newcastle striker Nick Woltemade as a potential long-term successor to Harry Kane. (Ekrem Konur)

- Arsenal have no intention of allowing midfielder Martin Zubimendi to leave in the January transfer window, despite interest from Chelsea and Real Madrid. (Football Insider)

- Barcelona scouts have been tracking Djurgarden attacking midfielder Bo Hegland, who has registered 10 goals and 18 assists in 29 matches for the Swedish side. (Expressen)

- Bayern Munich admire Liverpool playmaker Florian Wirtz, but are not actively pursuing a transfer at present. (Christian Falk)

- Leeds United have put contract negotiations on ice with forward Lukas Nmecha, leaving his long-term future at the club uncertain. (TEAMtalk)

- Manchester United winger Noah Ajayi, 17, is set to sign his first professional contract with the club after impressing at youth level. (Sky Sports)

- A host of major European clubs including Real Madrid, Barcelona, Liverpool, Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City, and PSG are tracking Bayern Munich talent Lennart Karl. (Ekrem Konur)

stories.headline: Max Verstappen wins Max vs 100 in style after overtaking 100 go-karters in 35 minutes
stories.summary: Max Verstappen stormed through a field of 100 karters to win Max vs 100 in remarkable fashion as the four-time Formula 1 world champion made light work of the unique challenge at Silverstone.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen stormed through a field of 100 karters to win Max vs 100 in remarkable fashion as the four-time Formula 1 world champion made light work of the unique challenge at Silverstone.

Verstappen was given 30 laps, or 75 minutes, to overtake 100 drivers from the back of the grid in a go-kart race but only needed 14 laps, and 35 minutes, to add the latest win to his motorsport collection.

The event was streamed live globally on ESPN on Disney+.

- As it happened: Relive Max vs 100 as Verstappen took on 10 karters

- HIGHLIGHTS: Watch the best bits from Max vs 100 on ESPN's YouTube

On a modified karting circuit at the home of F1 in the UK, Verstappen -- after starting 101st -- overtook 63 drivers on the very first lap, including ESPN's Nate Saunders, who barely lasted 10 seconds. Drivers clashed, spun around and ultimately watched Verstappen sail past as the predicted carnage ensued on Lap 1, resulting in waved yellow flags.

After that, Verstappen continued to carve his way through the field at an alarming rate, while also speaking to the competitors -- made up of athletes, content creators, journalists and other celebrities -- along the way.

"I'm coming for you," he said to a contestant at one stage. Later, he told commentators: "They need to focus because I'm definitely catching them."

It took Verstappen 15 minutes to get up to P7, and while at that stage he was still 14 seconds behind the runaway top three -- journalist Jacky Martens, YouTuber Zac Alsop and Red Bull's own Lewis Osler -- he quickly gained at a rate of around three seconds-a-lap.

The top three were given an extra 'fast lap' -- a shortcut of the circuit -- but that wasn't enough to catch Verstappen and he completed the challenge in style on Lap 14.

"My first lap was quite incredible," Verstappen said afterwards. "There was a lot happening and actually a few cars got stuck and I always managed to be on the other side, so didn't get stuck.

"And that made me get like 60 people in the first lap. So that just helps a lot, getting through to the front."

Asked where the win ranks in his victories, he said: "I think this is the best one yet!"

Saunders, meanwhile, was less positive post-race comments -- but nonetheless was impressed by the Dutchman.

"That was all a bit of a blur," he said. "Shortly after the start I looked to my right and there was Max -- and then he was gone. The way he was able to zigzag through the crowd was crazy."

Verstappen will next be in action at F1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The Red Bull star is sixth in the drivers' championship.

stories.headline: Njoku, Nwosu, Emmanwori, and more - 10 NFL players of Nigerian origin to watch this season
stories.summary: The NFL has long had a significant African presence, but no country is represented quite like Nigeria.
stories.body:
The 2026 NFL season is underway, and Nigerians will once again have plenty of reasons to pay attention, with players of Nigerian origin spread across the league, from defending Super Bowl champions to established starters, and former high draft picks looking for breakout seasons.

The NFL has long had a significant African presence, but no country is represented quite like Nigeria. There are 137 players of African origin across NFL rosters and practice squads at the start of the 2026 season, representing 24 African countries, with Nigeria accounting for 93 of them, more than two-thirds of the total.

Liberia is a distant second with nine players, followed by Côte d'Ivoire with seven, Cameroon with six and Ghana with five.

Every NFL team has at least one player of African origin, while Nigerian representation stretches across 29 of the league's 32 teams. Only the Minnesota Vikings, New Orleans Saints and Arizona Cardinals do not have a player of Nigerian origin on their roster or practice squad.

No team has more than the New York Jets. The Jets have eight players of Nigerian origin, including one on the practice squad, with Olu Fashanu, Joseph Ossai and Lagos-born veteran David Onyemata among the most recognizable.

Those numbers help illustrate how dramatically Nigeria's footprint in American football has grown. The country's NFL connection is no longer represented by a handful of isolated success stories.

Nigerian-born players and the children of Nigerian immigrants now occupy positions across the league, from quarterbacks and offensive linemen to linebackers, defensive backs and pass rushers.

Some are already champions. Uchenna Nwosu and Nick Emmanwori helped the Seattle Seahawks win Super Bowl LX last season, while Moro Ojomo and Osa Odighizuwa enter this year on NFC teams with legitimate championship ambitions.

Foye Oluokun remains one of the league's most productive linebackers, while former high draft picks Olu Fashanu and David Ojabo enter potentially important seasons in their development as potential breakout candidates.

Jalen Milroe, whose playing time may be considerably more limited but whose position, Nigerian heritage and presence on the defending champions make his development particularly intriguing.

Several others could have a significant say in who is still playing when Super Bowl LXI arrives in Los Angeles on Feb. 14.

From the contenders to the challengers and potential breakout players, here are 10 NFL players of Nigerian origin to watch in 2026.

SUPER BOWL CONTENDERS
Uchenna Nwosu, Edge, Seattle Seahawks
There is probably no better place to start than Nwosu. He is an established NFL veteran, a Super Bowl champion and a significant contributor on a Seattle team trying to win consecutive titles.

Nwosu played 16 games last season and recorded seven sacks, his best total since registering 9.5 in 2022.

He played 33 defensive snaps in Seattle's season-opening 13-10 victory over New England, finishing with five tackles and a pass defended as the Seahawks began their title defense by beating the team they defeated in Super Bowl LX.

At 29, Nwosu is entering a stage where another strong season and another championship run would add considerably to an already successful NFL career.

Why watch: An established Nigerian-American pass rusher playing significant snaps for the defending champions.

Super Bowl chances: Excellent.

Nick Emmanwori, Safety, Seattle Seahawks
Nwosu may be the established veteran, but Emmanwori could eventually become the bigger star. The young safety made an immediate impact as a rookie, finishing runner-up for AP Defensive Rookie of the Year and helping Seattle win the Super Bowl.

At 6-foot-3, Emmanwori possesses unusual size and athleticism for a safety, allowing Seattle to deploy him in multiple roles rather than simply leaving him deep in the secondary.

The challenge now is the second season. Opposing offenses have a full year of film on him, while expectations are considerably higher than when he arrived in the league. An offseason ankle problem also makes his health worth monitoring early in the season.

If healthy, Emmanwori has an opportunity to establish himself among the league's emerging defensive stars.

Why watch: He could make the jump from outstanding rookie to one of the NFL's better young defensive backs.

Super Bowl chances: Excellent.

Moro Ojomo, DT, Philadelphia Eagles
Ojomo has taken a very different route than usual to the NFL. Born in Lagos, he moved to California with his family when he was 8, eventually starred at Texas and was selected by the Philadelphia Eagles in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL draft.

For players selected that late, simply sticking around is an achievement. Ojomo has done considerably more. He has developed into an increasingly important part of an Eagles defensive front featuring Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis, giving Philadelphia another source of interior pressure.

That development makes 2026 particularly interesting. Ojomo has already gone from seventh-round project to legitimate NFL contributor. Another step Up the ladder could make him a much more recognizable name beyond Philadelphia.

Why watch: One of the best development stories among Nigerian-born players in the NFL and now an important piece on a championship contender.

Super Bowl chances: Very good.

Osa Odighizuwa, DT, San Francisco 49ers
There are flashier names on this list, but few have been more dependable. Odighizuwa played all 17 games in each of his final four seasons with the Dallas Cowboys before moving to San Francisco, establishing himself as one of the league's more durable interior defensive linemen.

Odighizuwa also comes from a football family. His older brother Owamagbe played in the NFL and now Osa arrives in San Francisco with an obvious assignment.

The 49ers recorded an NFL-low 20 sacks last season and needed additional help for a defensive front that had lost some of its previous dominance. Odighizuwa provides an established interior presence alongside Nick Bosa.

His first game suggested that the opportunity will be substantial this season. He started at defensive tackle and recorded two tackles as San Francisco's defense overwhelmed the Rams in a 27-7 season-opening victory in Melbourne. They limited the Rams to just seven points and 290 total yards, forced two turnovers, and limited Matthew Stafford to 155 passing yards

With fellow starting tackle Alfred Collins lost for the season with a torn patellar tendon, Odighizuwa is now an even more important part of a 49ers defensive front attempting to return to its old standards.

Why watch: Proven durability, substantial playing time and a new role on a team expecting to contend.

Super Bowl chances: Very good.

CHALLENGERS
Michael Onwenu, OL, New England Patriots
Onwenu already knows how close the Patriots came. New England's 2025 season carried them all the way to Super Bowl LX before Seattle ended the run with a 29-13 victory.

Onwenu remains one of New England's most important offensive linemen and has provided valuable versatility throughout his career, playing both guard and tackle. His role becomes even more important with quarterback Drake Maye established as the centerpiece of the Patriots offense.

Onwenu began 2026 where he left off, starting at right guard as New England's rebuilt offensive line allowed just two sacks against Seattle in its 13-10 opening-night loss.

The Patriots still had problems dealing with Seattle's pressure, particularly late, but Onwenu remains the established presence on an offensive line charged with protecting Maye as New England attempts to return to the Super Bowl.

Why watch: An established Nigerian-American starter protecting one of the AFC's leading young quarterbacks.

Super Bowl chances: Very good.

David Njoku, TE, Los Angeles Chargers
Njoku provides something this Nigerian group otherwise lacks: an established offensive skill-position player, having built a substantial NFL career as an athletic receiving tight end and now begins a new chapter with the Los Angeles Chargers.

His production dipped last season, when he caught 33 passes for 293 yards and four touchdowns in 12 games, making his fresh start alongside Justin Herbert particularly interesting.

Why watch: A proven offensive player getting a fresh start with one of the NFL's established quarterbacks.

Super Bowl chances: Good.

Foye Oluokun, LB, Jacksonville Jaguars
If playing time and production were the only criteria, Oluokun would be much higher.

The linebacker has been one of the NFL's most prolific tacklers, including league-leading totals of 192 with Atlanta in 2021 and 184 in his first season with Jacksonville.

Oluokun is an established every-down linebacker and a central figure in Jacksonville's defense.

Why watch: Perhaps the safest bet among this entire group to accumulate substantial playing time and production.

Super Bowl chances: Outside chance.

POTENTIAL BREAKOUTS
Olu Fashanu, OT, New York Jets
The Jets selected Olumuyiwa Fashanu in the first round of the 2024 draft after an outstanding college career at Penn State, viewing the Nigerian-American tackle as a potential long-term cornerstone of their offensive line.

Eventually, draft position has to translate into production, and it is about time for that developmental period to give way to expectation.

Fashanu possesses the size, footwork and pedigree that made him one of the premier offensive-line prospects in his draft class. Now he needs to establish himself as a high-level NFL starter.

Why watch: Former first-round talent approaching a potentially defining stage of his development.

Super Bowl chances: It is the Jets...

David Ojabo, Edge, Miami Dolphins
Few players on this list have a wider range of possible outcomes than Ojabo. Born in Port Harcourt, Ojabo spent part of his childhood in Nigeria before moving to Scotland and eventually the United States.

He took up American football relatively late but developed so quickly at Michigan that he was projected as a potential first-round pick before tearing his Achilles at his pro day.

Injuries repeatedly interrupted his career in Baltimore, and Miami now provides another opportunity. At 26, there is still time to show that the physical talent which once made him one of college football's most intriguing edge defenders can translate consistently to the NFL.

Why watch: This could be a pivotal season for one of the most naturally talented Nigerian-born players in the league.

Super Bowl chances: Low.

Jalen Milroe, QB, Seattle Seahawks
Milroe is the wildcard of this selection. Incidentally, not many are even aware that he has Nigerian heritage, and only a deep dive into his full name, Jalen Oluwaseun Isaiah Milroe, would give it away.

His position, as one of only two quarterbacks of Nigerian origin in the league - the other being former Kansas City practice squad QB Chris Oladokun, who is now a free agent - makes his development worth following.

Milroe is not Seattle's starting quarterback, meaning he could play considerably fewer snaps than anybody else in this top 10. But he did get minutes last season, and quarterbacks operate under different rules.

Milroe's exceptional running ability gives Seattle the possibility of using him in specialized packages, while his longer-term development could eventually determine whether he gets an opportunity to become an NFL starter.

Why watch: A quarterback of Nigerian heritage with exceptional physical tools developing on the roster of the NFL champions.

Super Bowl chances: Excellent as a member of Seattle, although his individual role could be limited.

HONORABLE MENTIONS
Boye Mafe, Edge, Cincinnati Bengals: The Nigerian-American pass rusher leaves Seattle with a Super Bowl ring and joins a Cincinnati team capable of making noise in the AFC.

Odafe Oweh, Edge, Washington Commanders: Oweh is one of the more physically gifted pass rushers in the league. His cross-town move from Baltimore gives him another opportunity to translate those tools into consistent production.

Joseph Ossai, Edge, New York Jets: Lagos-born Ossai has shown disruptive ability without yet producing consistently enough to become a leading NFL edge defender.

David Onyemata, DT, New York Jets: Born in Lagos and introduced to organized American football after moving to Canada for university, Onyemata has fashioned a remarkable decade-long NFL career.

Olu Oluwatimi, C, Seattle Seahawks: Oluwatimi appeared in eight regular-season games with four starts before playing in all three games of Seattle's postseason championship run. He begins 2026 behind the starters, but could become important if injuries create an opportunity.

stories.headline: Messi nets 100th Miami goal en route to Campeones Cup win
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in all competitions after heading home the opener in a 2-0 win over Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Lionel Messi scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in all competitions after heading home the opener in a 2-0 win over Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.

Messi's goal put Miami up 1-0 in the annual match between the champion of MLS and Liga MX before a late header from Casemiro put the game away to hand new coach Cristian "Kily" González a trophy in his first match in charge.

"Leo [Messi] told me I was going to become a champion, and he made it happen," González said.

"Moving forward, this gives us a huge morale boost, it's a vital element for us, and while we've achieved this, we have to keep going."

Luis Suárez set up the opener in the 24th minute with a perfectly lofted cross from the right side that Messi ran onto, outjumping his marker and scoring a rare goal with his head.

González led his first training session with Inter Miami on Tuesday after landing in Miami from Argentina earlier in the morning. The team had reached an agreement with González to replace interim coach Guillermo Hoyos on Aug. 27, but he was unable to take over until receiving his work permit.

His first game as Miami coach will be one to remember with Messi scoring his 100th goal for the club and the team picking up a trophy on the night.

"It's become a normality [for Messi] but it isn't," Rodrigo de Paul said about his Miami teammate.

"We have to enjoy him, admire him, see him with the love that he plays each game. Luckily, I've had him by my side for many years. I try to enjoy him to the maximum."

Messi, a World Cup winner in 2022, reached the milestone in only 115 games for Inter Miami, marking the quickest he has recorded 100 goals for any team he has represented. Messi previously reached the mark with Barcelona in 188 games and 174 games with Argentina.

Since joining Miami in 2023, Messi has 76 goals in MLS, 14 in Leagues Cup action, eight in the Concacaf Champions Cup and one at the FIFA Club World Cup.

Messi made an instant impact in south Florida since signing with Miami, leading the Herons to the 2023 Leagues Cup title just weeks after marking his debut against Cruz Azul -- the team against which he scored his first Miami goal.

The Inter Miami captain also guided the team to the 2024 Supporters' Shield -- setting the record for most points (74) in an MLS season -- and starred in the playoffs during a run to the 2025 MLS Cup title last year.

Messi has now scored 929 goals for club and country during his career and leads MLS with 19 goals in 22 games so far this season.

stories.headline: Jets suspend Connor Hellebuyck for failure to report to camp
stories.summary: The Jets on Wednesday night suspended star goalie Connor Hellebuyck for failure to report to the team's training camp.
stories.body:
The Winnipeg Jets on Wednesday night suspended star goalie Connor Hellebuyck for failure to report to training camp.

The Jets, who open camp Thursday in Winnipeg, Manitoba, didn't disclose how long the suspension would last. General manager Kevin Cheveldayoff will meet with reporters Thursday morning, the team said.

The suspension is the latest development in an ongoing saga that stems from Hellebuyck's desire to leave the franchise that drafted him in 2012.

In a statement issued through his agent, Ray Petkau, in late August, the 2025 NHL MVP and three-time Vezina Trophy winner asked to be traded. Hellebuyck said he "tried to handle the situation quietly and respectfully while giving the organization time to explore its options."

"My position has not changed, and I believe moving on is the best path forward for me and my family," Hellebuyck said in the statement. "... [I] hope a resolution can be reached soon."

In the weeks since that statement, there has been additional attention on the Jets to see how they would navigate the situation a season after missing the playoffs. Winnipeg finished eight points out of the second and final Western Conference wild-card spot a year after having the NHL's best record.

Several reasons contributed to the Jets missing the playoffs for the first time in three years, including an extended absence for Hellebuyck.

The 33-year-old underwent a minor arthroscopic procedure in late November and sat out about a month. Winnipeg went 3-10-1 in his absence after starting the season 11-7.

Hellebuyck finished the season 23-23-11 with a 2.86 goals-against average and an .895 save percentage. His GAA was his highest since the 2021-22 season (2.97); his save percentage was the worst of his career after never previously finishing below .900.

He did guide the United States to its first Olympic goal medal since 1980 in February.

The Jets will open camp with six goalies on their roster, with Hellebuyck among those listed.

Stuart Skinner, who signed a two-year contract worth $3.75 million annually in free agency, has the most NHL experience of the group, apart from Hellebuyck. Skinner went 23-17-9 with a 2.92 GAA and a .888 save percentage last season, which he started with the Edmonton Oilers before being traded to the Pittsburgh Penguins. He was part of the Oilers teams that reached consecutive Stanley Cup finals in 2024 and 2025 before losing to the Florida Panthers.

Thomas Milic is the only other current Jets goalie who played in the NHL last season. Milic, 23, was 0-1 with a 3.46 GAA and a .871 save percentage in three games after spending the majority of 2025-26 playing in the AHL for the Manitoba Moose.

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: Alexa Grasso shows off flyweight's elite status in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
It's uncommon for two fighters ranked in the pound-for-pound top 10 to meet in a bout with no championship at stake. But that was the case at Saturday's fourth annual Noche UFC, where Alexa Grasso faced Manon Fiorot.

Grasso is a former women's flyweight champion and Fiorot competed for the belt last year, so their status as MMA elites was well established before they fought. And when Grasso won by unanimous decision, she further solidified her standing in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

The top five of the rankings remains intact, and Grasso moves up from 10th to replace Fiorot at No. 6. Fiorot slips two positions to No. 8 in a pound-for-pound hierarchy in which seven of the 10 ranked women compete at flyweight (including Zhang Weili, the former UFC strawweight champion who last fought in an unsuccessful challenge of Valentina Shevchenko in November).

With Shevchenko injured and having vacated her title, there will be much scrambling for the top spot, which will be at stake when No. 5 Natalia Silva fights unranked Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 16. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Cris Cyborg; 5. Alexa Grasso; 6. Manon Fiorot; 7. Dakota Ditcheva; 8. Natalia Silva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Zhang; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Blanchfield; 8. Ditcheva; 9. Suarez; 10. Fiorot.

Dre Waters: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Fiorot; 10. Suarez.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Ditcheva.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

5. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

6. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Alexandre Pantoja

UFC flyweight

Record: 30-6

Last: L (TKO1) vs. Joshua Van, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Sept. 19 vs. Joshua Van

Pantoja became the UFC's unquestioned flyweight king by racking up four title defenses, including two in pay-per-view main events in 2024. He built his winning streak to eight in his UFC 317 win over Kai Kara-France, whom he had already defeated before, like other challengers. But he lost his belt in a gruesome way, injuring his elbow in the opening seconds of a UFC 323 fight with Van. Pantoja gets his rematch with Van at UFC 331.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight interim champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was heralded as the future of the generation when he broke onto the scene, but endured growing pains in losses to Ngannou and Jones. He looks formidable now, and no one will be counting him out if he faces Aspinall in a title unification bout.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight / light heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: TBA

He was on the verge of making history when the opportunity fell apart. Pereira was a UFC champion at middleweight, then light heavyweight, but his unprecedented pursuit of a belt in a third weight class did not go well for the Brazilian, who lost an interim heavyweight title fight to Gane on the White House card. At 39 years old, Pereira does not have much time left to recapture the magic.

Other fighters receiving votes: Joshua Van and Arman Tsarukyan.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail semifinals: Bulldogs move to lock away rising rookie
stories.summary: Ronaldo Mulitalo is determined to honour his departing Sharks teammates, Sione Katoa has opened up about his future at the Cowboys and his finals days at the Sharks, while Nathan Cleary is fighting the clock to be fit for Penrith's prelim.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's semifinal week.

Bulldogs move early to lock down rising forward

The Bulldogs have moved early to lock down rising forward Alekolasimi 'AJ' Jones, with the club's Rookie of the Year agreeing to a two-year contract extension.

ESPN understands Jones, who was already contracted through the 2027 season, has agreed to a new deal that will keep him at Belmore beyond his existing contract.

The move ensures Jones' future is secured before he would have been free to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 from November 1.

Kennedy backs Hynes amid criticism

Will Kennedy believes Nicho Hynes has grown from the criticism that has followed him throughout his career, praising the Sharks star ahead of their semi-final against the Roosters.

"He's learned a lot from all the criticism he gets and he's taken a step forward," Kennedy said. "For me, I just want to get around him because he's my brother and I want to play next to him."

Trindall 'really good' after shoulder scare

Will Kennedy says Braydon Trindall has pulled up well after battling through a shoulder issue in Cronulla's finals win over North Queensland.

Kennedy said Trindall had been "really dialled in on the mental side" of his game and indicated the halfback had told him he was feeling "really good" ahead of the Roosters clash.

Mulitalo relishing 'Marky Mark' rematch

Ronaldo Mulitalo is embracing another blockbuster battle with Roosters star Mark Nawaqanitawase, describing the departing winger as a "generational talent".

Mulitalo said Nawaqanitawase "brings the best out of me" and revealed their on-field rivalry is largely one-sided when it comes to the verbal exchanges.

"He's a gentleman out there... he doesn't really say anything. I think it's more myself," Mulitalo joked. "He knows I'm just going to keep talking, so he just ignores me anyway."

Mulitalo determined to honour departing Sharks

Ronaldo Mulitalo says Cronulla's finals run carries added significance with several longtime teammates set to leave the club at season's end.

Mulitalo said he has played alongside some of the departing Sharks since he was 16 and wants to "honour those boys" with his performance against the Roosters.

"I don't want to let them down and disappoint them, winning the game is the most important part of the week for me."

Katoa reveals Cowboys appeal

Sione Katoa has revealed North Queensland's attacking style was a major attraction behind his move to the Cowboys in 2027.

After helping eliminate his future club from the finals, Katoa told ESPN he "loves the style of footy" they play, describing it as "free footy" and similar to Cronulla's attack.

Katoa emotional over Sharks farewell
He also admitted the reality that every game could be his last for Cronulla is beginning to sink in.

"Tonight might have been the last week, maybe the last game," he told ESPN after scoring a double against North Queensland.

"I'm very happy right now that I get another week with my brothers and play again."

Cleary racing clock for preliminary final

Nathan Cleary is in doubt for Penrith's preliminary final after scans revealed an stress-related bone issue in his foot.

The Panthers will assess and monitor their star halfback over the next fortnight, with their week off providing valuable recovery time.

Cleary has, however, been cleared of any suspension concern after receiving only a Grade 1 Dangerous Contact charge for his incident with Hugo Savala.

stories.headline: Man United's collapse puts Carrick under pressure for first time
stories.summary: After being eliminated by Brighton & Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup, Manchester United boss Michael Carrick is now facing the first real pressure of his reign.
stories.body:
MANCHESTER, England -- Michael Carrick isn't the first Manchester United manager to go through a crisis, but this is now the first of his reign.

Carrick's team led 2-0 against Brighton & Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup third round on Wednesday and somehow conspired to lose 3-2.

Coming in the immediate aftermath of a controversial but still abject derby defeat to 10-man Manchester City and 24 hours after their best young player, JJ Gabriel, made it clear he wants to leave, it capped a disastrous few days at Old Trafford.

United's players attempted to applaud the fans at the final whistle, but were engulfed by boos as they slowly lapped the pitch. As red shirts disappeared down the tunnel, they were followed by chants of "What the f------ h--- was that?"

"I totally understand the feelings of the supporters," said Carrick after the match.

"We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It's on me ultimately. We can't accept that as a group. I take responsibility for it. The performance towards the end of the second half, that's on me.

"We'll all be better. We have to be better. We want to win and want to win quickly."

There are certain results which haunt United managers. For Erik Ten Hag, it was the calamitous FA Cup semifinal against English League Championship side Coventry City.

Ruben Amorim will forever be remembered for the UEFA Europa League final defeat to Tottenham Hotspur and the Carabao Cup exit to League Two side Grimsby Town. Carrick can only hope that this doesn't stick in the memory in the same way.

The 45-year-old has enjoyed a relatively serene 11 months in charge after taking over from Amorim -- initially temporarily -- in January. Playing one match a week during the second half of last season, United won 12 of the 17 games to climb to third in the Premier League table and secure a return to the UEFA Champions League.

But any hope that the positive momentum might carry over into the new campaign has disappeared within the first month. It's now two wins from six games and four points from four in the league. For the first time, Carrick is under real pressure. The fallout of the defeat to Brighton makes for painful reading.

United lost at Old Trafford after leading by two goals for the first time in 50 years. It was their first defeat at home after leading at halftime since May 1984.

They haven't won a domestic cup tie since beating Leicester City in the FA Cup in February 2025. It's now four domestic cup defeats in a row under three different managers -- Amorim, Darren Fletcher and Carrick. Brighton have won the last two after winning here in the FA Cup in January. They're never far away from a United catastrophe.

After 10 minutes, the 900 fans who made the 500-mile round trip to Manchester were perhaps wishing they hadn't. Fabian Hürzeler made six changes to the team that beat Coventry 5-0 on Sunday and it looked to have backfired when Shea Lacey and Mason Mount put United 2-0 up.

The story of the night should have been one academy graduate -- 19-year-old Lacey -- showing another -- 15-year-old Gabriel -- that Old Trafford is the place to be. But it wasn't.

Charalampos Kostoulas gave the visitors hope with a goal just before halftime. What followed was a limp and lifeless second-half performance from United, and Brighton equalized through Pascal Gross.

United defended so badly all night that there was a sense of inevitability that Brighton would score again, and it came just three minutes later from substitute Maxim De Cuyper. The Seagulls have now won on five of their last six visits to Old Trafford.

"I definitely believed and belief was a big word in the preparation for us," said Hürzeler.

"When you go to a place like here, you need to have belief and then to show it when you are 2-0 down shows real character."

Hürzeler and Brighton are preparing to mark their 125th anniversary when Arsenal visit the Amex on Saturday. Carrick may well be less enthusiastic about his weekend plans. The trip to Fulham on Sunday looks increasingly awkward. Álvaro Arbeloa's team are yet to win in the league this season, but earned a creditable draw at Liverpool last time out.

Beyond the extended international break, there's a tricky run of fixtures including Tottenham at home, Atlético Madrid away and Leeds United away.

"We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for," said Carrick.

"We're out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches. The next game is Sunday. That's all I'm thinking about right now."

Carrick will need to find a solution somewhere. Previous United managers have seen results unravel very quickly. Just ask Ten Hag and Amorim. Once the pressure grows and the spotlight intensifies, it can be very hard to turn things around.

It's the task that Carrick now faces. For the first time in his tenure he's facing serious questions. It's up to him to find the answers.

stories.headline: Max vs 100: Verstappen jokes taking on '200' drivers next time after winning crazy challenge
stories.summary: Max Verstappen has joked that he's ready to race 200 drivers next after storming from the back of a 101-grid to take victory in his half his allotted time in Max vs 100 on Wednesday.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen has joked that he's ready to race 200 drivers next after storming from the back of a 101-grid to take victory in his half his allotted time in Max vs 100 on Wednesday.

Verstappen needed just 14 laps, and 35 minutes, to complete the challenge, which was broadcast live globally on ESPN on Disney+.

The unique go-karting race represented the latest of the four-time world champions' side quests away from Formula 1 and the Red Bull driver is already looking ahead to his next test.

"Yeah, that's what I said before ... I was like maybe 200 [drivers] and then we'll see again," he told the media after the race at Silverstone.

The event took place on a custom-built track, a mix of two different circuits: 1.3km of permanent karting track on the Silverstone infield, with another 1.15km of temporary track added specifically for this event.

He was given 30 laps, or 75 minutes, to get the job done against athletes, content creators, journalists and other celebrities, and he ended up exceeding everyone's expectations, including his own.

Verstappen managed to pass 63 drivers on the very first lap and when he was asked if he had a strategy heading into the race, he said: "I mean, when I was walking to the grid and I saw where I had to start it's like oof, that's a very far way back. But after my first lap I was like I think we're all right, I think we're good.

"It was mainly just depending on the first two laps, that's why I was like OK if I clear the first two laps, what can it be like at 15-20 laps. But yeah, I think the first lap went a bit better than expected, so that helps a lot.

- Max Verstappen wins Max vs 100 in style after overtaking 100 go-karters in 35 minutes

- Max vs 100: Highlights, commentary as Verstappen beats 100 go-karters - as it happened

- Max vs 100: How Verstappen's karting years made an F1 champion - and prepared him for an all-new test

"The first lap is just chaos so you just want to survive and then after that it's a bit like you're just hunting them down. So that's also quite nice where you have to just put the laps in by yourself and you catch them one by one.

"You just act on instinct, whatever happens when the lights go out, you kind of just see where the gaps are and then you also kind of need to trust the few people around you that they don't do anything crazy. But to be honest, they didn't."

He managed to clear the field but he spent several laps catching the top three -- journalist Jacky Martens, YouTuber Zac Alsop and Red Bull's own Lewis Osler.

Verstappen has always had fond memories of his karting days, and heading into the event he said the last time he raced in a "proper go-kart" was 2016.

"It's just great that with Red Bull they always come up with some crazy fun things and it suits me as well," he said.

"I can really be myself and I think also the way it was organised today, I know that it requires a lot of effort to be able to do something like this.

stories.headline: Browns-Buccaneers matchup Sunday is more than just Baker Mayfield facing his old team
stories.summary: — Baker Mayfield has become the leader and face of the franchise the Cleveland Browns hoped for when they drafted him No. 1 overall in 2018.
stories.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- — Baker Mayfield has become the leader and face of the franchise the Cleveland Browns hoped for when they drafted him No. 1 overall in 2018.


The Buccaneers are glad he’s found a home in Tampa Bay.


What did the veteran quarterback learn in his four years in Cleveland?


“A lot of things. I think probably the biggest one (is) trying to be the same person each and every day for the guys in the locker room, the people you work with, the staff that you’re around each day, (and understanding) that some things are out of your control,” Mayfield said. “If you’re trying to get it fixed and you’re not worried about the football aspect of your job, you’re probably letting some things slide and fall by the wayside. So, I think controlling who I am each and every day, trying to lead the best way possible and control the offense and, yeah, ultimately win.”


There’s more to the Browns-Buccaneers matchup Sunday than Mayfield facing his old team.


It’s two 0-1 teams looking to get on the winning track. Expectations are much different for both.


It’ll be a surprise if the Browns don’t finish last in a tough AFC North. The Buccaneers play in the weak NFC South where all four teams lost their openers.


“I think we got the bad taste out of our mouths,” Bucs receiver Emeka Egbuka said. “We’re ready to capitalize on Sunday. This new opportunity that we’ve been given. First game in the home stadium. Looking forward to seeing the Krewe and all the fans out there. Hopefully we’ll put on a show.”


The Browns are giving Deshaun Watson a second start with Shedeur Sanders watching from the sideline and waiting for an opportunity that could arrive when the team plays its first home game next week.


For now, it’s Watson’s team and the beleaguered QB is running out of chances to prove he can be the Pro Bowl player the Browns gave up a ton of picks to acquire four years ago.


“I always expect our players to play well; I wouldn’t put them out there if I didn’t,” Browns coach Todd Monken said. “So, I expect him to play really well. There was moments Sunday that he did, and there were moments we did a really good job offensively, and there were moments we didn’t. There were moments we didn’t coach well enough; there were moments we didn’t play well enough.”


Need to know
Cleveland (0-1) at Tampa Bay (0-1) in Tampa, Fla.


When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, CBS


Latest odds: Buccaneers by 8 1/2


Against the spread: Browns 0-1; Buccaneers 0-1.


Last week: Browns lost to the Jaguars 34-10; Buccaneers lost to the Bengals 33-27.


Last meeting: Browns beat the Buccaneers 23-17 in overtime on Nov. 27, 2022 in Cleveland.


Series record: Browns lead 7-4.


Matchup to watch
Buccaneers WR Emeka Egbuka vs. Browns secondary. Egbuka had five catches for 63 yards against the Bengals. Mayfield targeted him on the first three plays of the game and just missed on an opportunity for a deep TD pass in that first series. Browns five-time Pro Bowl cornerback Denzel Ward will primarily cover Egbuka when he lines up wide right. Cleveland used man coverage on 38% of snaps in a 34-10 loss to Jacksonville. Egbuka, who has had success against man coverage in his brief career, could go against Tyson Campbell or Myles Harden depending where he lines up.


Stats and stuff
— Browns QB Deshaun Watson completed 16 of 22 for 205 yards, one TD and rushed for 38 yards in Week 1. He also threw a pick.


— Browns rookie WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion combined for 102 yards receiving and a TD for Boston.


— LB Carson Schwesinger, the 2025 AP NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year, led team with 10 tackles and had one tackle for loss in Week 1.


— Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield was 23 of 28 for 216 yards with one rushing TD and three fumbles lost.


— Buccaneers RB Bucky Irving had 93 scrimmage yards and one TD last week.


— Buccaneers rookie LB Josiah Trotter had a pick-6 on Joe Burrow in his NFL debut.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 37
Goals: 33
Assists: 15

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.
